title: UDF dev kit
tagline: Python and Rust UDFs on the local database, proven with a smoke test.
role: A local Exasol Personal database ships with no script language container, so no Python or Rust UDF runs until one is installed, and it has no BucketFS upload service. The UDF dev kit drives the Exasol launcher's container commands for you - the official Python container, the kit's prebuilt machine-learning one (scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, scipy) picked for your database's architecture and version and verified against its pinned digest, the pinned Rust container (proven by the kit's prebuilt Rust smoke UDF, which reports the container, rustc and exasol-udf-sdk versions against the pin), or one built from your requirements - checks every Python install with a UDF that reports each package's version against the pin, and copies files a UDF reads into BucketFS: model files with their digest recorded (exakit model put), scored by a UDF made from its template (exakit model template).
installed_by: exakit marketplace udf-devkit, or the ml-engineer persona. Installing it prepares the official Python container and the pinned PYTHON3_ML container with scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy and SciPy. EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE=rust also prepares RUST and proves it with its smoke UDF. Each container installation can restart the database; existing ML packages are checked without reinstalling. Missing packages fail the add-on and name the retry.
platforms: macOS on Apple silicon, Linux (x86_64 and Arm, including WSL) and Windows x86_64. Needs the Exasol launcher 2.3.0 or later; update a kit-owned launcher with exakit update personal; update a user-owned launcher with its original installer. Building your own container (exakit udf-build) also needs a running Docker or Podman engine (the Podman the launcher installs counts) and the notebook add-on.

quickstart.note: The official Python 3.12 container, alias PYTHON3. The database restarts once.

The prebuilt container for your database (scikit-learn, pandas, numpy, scipy at the versions in versions.json), downloaded once, verified, alias PYTHON3_ML; the smoke UDF checks each version against the pin. The database restarts once. Packages it lacks: exakit udf-build requirements.txt (alias PYTHON3_CUSTOM; needs Docker or Podman and the notebook add-on).
Prints the path the UDF opens, under /buckets.

quickstart.step: Score with a model trained elsewhere
quickstart.note: Records its digest and prints its /buckets path; exakit model template shows how to create the scoring UDF for it.

commands.summary: Install the official Python container (or the Rust one) and prove it.
commands.description: python (the default, or EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE): the launcher's official Python 3.12 container, alias PYTHON3, then the smoke UDF. rust: the pinned Rust container from the matrix in versions.json for your database's architecture and version, downloaded once into the cache, verified against its sha256 and size, installed as alias RUST (one already there is proven without a reinstall; --force reinstalls), then proven by the kit's Rust smoke UDF: the row's smoke_asset (libexakit_smoke.so built by CI for your architecture with the container's rustc 1.98.1 and exasol-udf-sdk 0.33.0) is shipped for both architectures and verified against its sha256 BEFORE the install, copied into the bucket directory as udf/libexakit_smoke.so, registered as STARTER_KIT.EXAKIT_SMOKE(x BIGINT) RETURNS VARCHAR(2000) AS %udf_object /buckets/bfsdefault/default/udf/libexakit_smoke.so and run once; it answers the container, rustc and sdk versions, which are held against the row (--json smoke: container, rustc, sdk, rustc_full). --force reinstalls the Python container too. --json prints one object: {"ok": true, "language", "alias", "container": {"url", "sha256", "arch", "db_versions"} (null fields for the launcher's own container), "smoke": [{"package", "version"}]} or {"ok": false, "language", "step", "reason", "remedy"} with step one of select-container, download, verify, install, smoke.

exit_codes.0: the container is installed and, for Python, the smoke UDF passed
exit_codes.2: bad arguments: a language that is not python or rust, an unknown option
exit_codes.3: the smoke UDF found a declared package missing
exit_codes.4: no container in the matrix for this language, architecture or database version, or the downloaded file does not match its pinned digest (removed; run again)
exit_codes.5: not ready: the add-on is not installed, the database is not running, the launcher is older than 2.3.0, the download did not arrive, the install was not confirmed, no bucket directory to put the Rust smoke library into
exit_codes.6: the launcher could not install the container (exakit logs)
exit_codes.7: the smoke UDF did not run, or reported a version other than the pinned one (Rust: the rustc or exasol-udf-sdk differ, both named; or the container refused the library with F-UDF-CL-RUST-9001, its ABI fingerprint SDK_VERSION:RUSTC_VERSION not matching the container's; or the row's smoke library is not pinned yet)

commands.summary: Install the prebuilt container for this database, or your own, or list them.
commands.description: default: the matrix row (versions.json, components.udf-devkit.containers) for the language, your DATABASE's architecture (an Apple-silicon Mac runs an aarch64 database, Windows an x86_64 one) and its version; downloaded once into $EXAKIT_HOME/cache/containers (EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR, a folder or base URL, instead of the release), verified against its pinned sha256 and size before the launcher sees it, installed as PYTHON3_ML (python) or RUST (rust; an installed RUST is updated); the Python smoke UDF compares every package's version with the pin, the Rust one (see udf-setup) the container's rustc and exasol-udf-sdk. A Rust tarball of your own is installed, not proven: the Rust smoke library is built for the kit's pinned container only. A tarball of yours is installed under --alias (PYTHON3_CUSTOM unless named) and proven the same way. --list shows the launcher's containers and which are installed. --json: the same objects and exit codes as udf-setup.

exit_codes.2: bad arguments: not a tarball, not a file, a bad alias, a language that is not python or rust
exit_codes.3: the smoke UDF found a declared package missing
exit_codes.4: no container for this language, architecture or database version, or a digest mismatch (the file is removed; run again)
exit_codes.5: not ready: the add-on, the database, the launcher, the download or the disk; or not confirmed
exit_codes.6: the launcher could not install the container (exakit logs)
exit_codes.7: the smoke UDF did not run, or reported a version other than the pinned one (Rust: see udf-setup)

commands.summary: Start or stop the local MLflow server, show its address, or replay pending runs.
commands.description: The server listens on 127.0.0.1, starting at port 5000. Its SQLite store, artifacts, log and pending run spool live under ~/.exasol-starter-kit/mlflow. The notebook add-on supplies the client and the UDF dev kit enables the service. Starting installs the full MLflow server package into the notebook environment if needed. Starting it records that you want it: exakit start brings it back after that, and never starts it for a udf-devkit user who has not asked for it. A plain stop is for the session; exakit mlflow disable (or stop --disable) stops it and keeps it off until the next exakit mlflow start. exakit stop stops the server; exakit logs mlflow shows its log. Replay sends spooled runs to MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI, the kit server, or the local store, and removes only records logged successfully.

parameters.name: <action>
parameters.description: Choose the server operation, or replay pending MLflow run records.

parameters.name: --port N
parameters.description: start only: loopback port for a new MLflow server. An already-running server keeps its current port.

parameters.name: --disable
parameters.description: stop only: also prevent automatic restart with exakit start. The disable action has the same effect.

parameters.name: --json
parameters.description: Print the action result as JSON.

parameters.name: --tracking-uri URI
parameters.description: replay only: send pending records to this MLflow server.

parameters.name: --tracking-dir PATH
parameters.description: replay only: log to a local MLflow store in this folder.

parameters.name: --timeout SECONDS
parameters.description: replay only: server health-check timeout.

parameters.name: --help, -h
parameters.description: Show this command reference; install nothing and change no services.

notes: First-time setup installs two large containers with database restarts. The ML archive alone is about 842 MB on Arm. The progress percentage is an estimate between setup milestones, not a measured download percentage. Keep the verified cache and installed aliases for subsequent runs; follow the install log with exakit logs setup -f.

Every container install restarts the database. You are asked first; --yes answers, and so does a run with no terminal. Running add-on services (dash-server, the scheduler) are stopped before and started again after.

The Python smoke UDF lives in the EXAKIT_UDF schema and is replaced on every install; the Rust one is STARTER_KIT.EXAKIT_SMOKE over udf/libexakit_smoke.so in the bucket directory, the same folder a Rust UDF of yours goes to (exakit rust-udf, the next kit step). Drop a schema if you want its smoke UDF gone; the next install creates it again.

The kit ships architecture-specific Rust smoke libraries with SHA-256 and size pins in versions.json. A matching bundled library is verified before use; a configured release or mirror asset is a verified fallback. Builds must use the pinned Linux image, rustc and Exasol SDK; a host macOS build is not a Linux UDF library.
Write a UDF for a container with its alias: CREATE OR REPLACE PYTHON3_ML SCALAR SCRIPT ... The official container answers to PYTHON3, the Rust one to RUST.

Containers: the prebuilt ones are a matrix in versions.json (components.udf-devkit.containers), one row per language and architecture with the database versions it runs on, its runtime (Python 3.12, rustc 1.98.1), the pinned packages or crates, url, sha256 and size. The row is chosen by the DATABASE's architecture (aarch64 on an Apple-silicon Mac, x86_64 on Windows and most Linux; EXAKIT_UDF_ARCH=x86_64|aarch64 overrides) and its version; a mismatch is refused (exit 4) rather than guessed. The digest is verified before any install; the file stays in $EXAKIT_HOME/cache/containers and is reused once verified. EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR (a folder, a file:// or https:// base URL holding the file by name) serves it offline. EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE=python|rust is the default language for the commands and the persona install.
Uninstalling the add-on leaves the containers in the database, because your UDFs may use them; exasol slc remove <alias> removes one.

Where BucketFS lives, the aliases, the schema and the build flavor (template-Exasol-all-python-3.12, from exasol/script-languages-release) are settings at the top of setup/lib/udf-devkit.sh and its PowerShell twin setup/lib/udf-devkit.ps1, so a launcher that moves them needs a kit update that changes those values, not new logic.

A new version of the UDF dev kit (a 2.0 included) arrives with exakit update, which records it and says when it is a major step. It never replaces a container your UDFs use: install the new prebuilt one when you are ready with exakit udf-use default.

troubleshooting.symptom: The UDF dev kit needs Exasol launcher 2.3.0 or later
troubleshooting.remedy: Check Owner in exakit version. Update a kit-owned launcher with exakit update personal; update a user-owned launcher with its original installer.

troubleshooting.symptom: The container does not match its pinned digest (exit 4, step verify)
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit udf-use default - the file was removed and is downloaded afresh; if it fails again the release asset changed and the kit needs an update

troubleshooting.symptom: No prebuilt container fits this database (exit 4, step select-container: no row for the architecture or the database version)
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit update - a newer kit may carry the row; until then exakit udf-build requirements.txt builds one for this machine

troubleshooting.symptom: The smoke UDF reported a version other than the pinned one (exit 7)
troubleshooting.remedy: The container answering to PYTHON3_ML is not the one the kit pinned: remove it from $EXAKIT_HOME/cache/containers and run exakit udf-use default again (exakit udf-use --list shows what is installed)

troubleshooting.symptom: Rust: the smoke UDF reported rustc X, pinned 1.98.1, or the container refused the library (F-UDF-CL-RUST-9001) - exit 7, step smoke
troubleshooting.remedy: The library in the cache was built for another toolchain than the RUST container: remove $EXAKIT_HOME/cache/containers/libexakit_smoke-<arch>.so and run exakit udf-setup --language rust again; if it repeats, the kit's versions.json pins a library that does not match its container - exakit update

troubleshooting.symptom: Rust: the smoke UDF library is not pinned in this kit's versions.json yet (exit 7, step smoke)
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit update - the RUST container is installed (exasol slc list) and usable; the kit proves it once a release carries the library's digest

troubleshooting.symptom: Rust: the smoke UDF library does not match its pinned digest (exit 4, step verify)
troubleshooting.remedy: exakit udf-setup --language rust - the file was removed and is downloaded afresh; the container was not touched

troubleshooting.symptom: Building a container needs a running container engine, Docker or Podman, and none answers
The database did not come back after the container install
exakit model put: a different file of that name is already there
exakit model list flags a model as CHANGED since it was put

environment.name: EXAKIT_UDF_LANGUAGE
environment.effect: Default python or rust; --language overrides it. Default python.

environment.name: EXAKIT_UDF_ARCH
environment.effect: Override the detected database architecture: x86_64 or aarch64. Normally leave unset.

environment.name: EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINERS_MIRROR
environment.effect: Local directory, file:// directory or HTTPS base URL containing the pinned assets. Size and SHA-256 checks still apply.

environment.name: EXAKIT_UDF_CONTAINER_CACHE
environment.effect: Container cache directory. Default $EXAKIT_HOME/cache/containers; retain it to avoid downloading the 842 MB ML archive again.

environment.name: EXAKIT_UDF_INSTALL_TIMEOUT
environment.effect: Seconds allowed for a launcher container installation. Default 3600; this is an install budget, not a download-speed setting.

environment.name: EXAKIT_MODEL_TRUST
environment.effect: Set to 1 to confirm the source of an unproven pickle/joblib model. Equivalent to model put --yes; unrelated to overwriting.

environment.name: MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI
environment.effect: Optional MLflow destination for notebook runs/replay. Leave unset to use the kit-managed service or local fallback.

environment.name: EXAKIT_MLFLOW_PORT
environment.effect: Preferred local MLflow port, default 5000. exakit mlflow start --port overrides it.
